note_claims.claim: The patient has had a cough and coryza for four days.
The patient has had increased work of breathing since yesterday.
The patient has had a temperature up to 37.9 °C.
The patient has had four wet nappies in 24 hours.
The patient has had an apnoea.
The patient has no cyanosis.
The patient was born at 39 weeks with no neonatal problems.
The patient has no cardiac or respiratory history.
The patient's immunisations are up to date.
The patient has taken Calpol once yesterday.
The patient has no known drug allergies.
The patient's temperature is 37.8 °C.
The patient's respiratory rate (RR) is 54 times a minute.
The patient's heart rate (HR) is 150.
The patient's oxygen level (SpO2) is 95 percent in air.
The patient exhibits intercostal and subcostal recession (pulling in between ribs and under them) when breathing.
The patient's capillary refill time (CRT) is under two seconds.
The patient is alert and looking around.
The patient has bilateral fine crackles and wheeze on both sides of his chest.
The clinical impression is Bronchiolitis with increased work of breathing (intercostal recession) and feeds about 50% of usual.
The plan is a same-day referral to the paediatric assessment unit.
The plan is to give the patient small, frequent feeds and saline nose drops before feeds in the meantime.
The patient is advised that the illness may worsen over the first three to five days.
The safety-netting advice is to call 999 if there are pauses in breathing, blue colour, or severe difficulty breathing on the way.
The safety-netting advice is to call the practice back if unable to attend within the hour to arrange an ambulance.

transcript_facts.fact: Arlo has had a runny nose and a cough for four days.
Arlo's breathing has been going really fast since yesterday.
Arlo is seven months old.
Arlo had a temperature of 37.9 °C this morning.
Arlo is taking most of his bottles.
Arlo is only managing about half of each bottle since yesterday.
The relative corrected the previous statement about feeding amount.
Arlo keeps pulling off to breathe.
Arlo has had four wet nappies in the last 24 hours.
Arlo usually has six or seven wet nappies.
The relative's sister had bronchiolitis two years ago, and she stopped breathing in the night, requiring an ambulance.
There was no history of similar events with Arlo.
Arlo has not gone blue or very pale.
Arlo brought up a bit of milk after coughing.
Arlo was born at 39 weeks with no problems.
Arlo has no heart or lung problems.
Arlo's immunisations are up to date.
Arlo has taken Calpol once yesterday.
The relative smokes outside but never in the house.
Arlo's temperature is 37.8 °C.
Arlo's respiratory rate is about 54 times a minute.
Arlo's heart rate is 150.
Arlo's oxygen level is 95 percent.
Arlo is pulling in between his ribs and under them when he breathes (working hard).
Arlo's capillary refill is under two seconds.
Arlo is alert and looking around.
The clinician heard crackles and some wheeze on both sides of Arlo's chest.
The findings fit with bronchiolitis, a common virus in babies.
The clinician recommended seeing Arlo at the hospital today.
The clinician will ring the paediatric team.
The paediatric team can keep an eye on his breathing, help with feeds, and give him oxygen or other treatment if needed.
The clinician advised giving Arlo smaller feeds more often until he gets to the hospital.
The clinician advised saline drops in his nose before feeds to help clear it.
Bronchiolitis often gets worse over the first three to five days before it gets better.
If on the way, the patient should call 999 if he has any pauses in his breathing, goes blue, or is really struggling to breathe.
The clinician advised the relative to go straight there from the clinic.
If the relative cannot get there within the hour, they should ring back and an ambulance will be arranged.
